newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt gains strong fillip at close from NZD rise.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt gains strong fillip at close from NZD rise.

* NZ debt rallies sharply at close as TWI breaks higher
* Flows very heavy in Sept futures, 7554 contracts traded
* Lack of curve flattening signals doubt over NZD rise
New Zealand debt rallied strongly across the curve at Wednesday's close on the back of a powerful rise in the kiwi dollar.
Physical short rates put in an impressive 22-basis point rally to 8.21 percent, while the September futures contract rose 21 pips to 92.20 on extremely solid volume of 7,554 contracts.
The New Zealand dollar shot to 64.99 on its Trade-Weighted Index, well up from its 64.64 Tuesday close, on the back of Australian dollar strength and some short-covering.

The Australian dollar initially slid when the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) announced it had cut its official cash rate by 50 basis points to five percent, but was quickly bought back as the market speculated there would not be a further credit easing in Australia in the near future.
By 5 p.m. NZ time (0500 GMT) the Australian dollar was quoted at US$0.7454/59 after dipping briefly to 0.7395 immediately after the RBA announcement.
The New Zealand dollar ended the day at US$0.6510/17, up from 0.6964/01 at the open and 0.6465/72 at Tuesday's close.
